lines: Τῶν καλῶν καὶ τιμίων τὴν εἴδησιν ὑπολαμβάνοντες, μᾶλλον
δ' ἑτέραν ἑτέρας ἢ κατ' ἀκρίβειαν ἢ τῷ βελτιόνων τε
καὶ θαυμασιωτέρων εἶναι, δι' ἀμφότερα ταῦτα τὴν περὶ τῆς ψυχῆς
ἱστορίαν εὐλόγως ἂν ἐν πρώτοις τιθείημεν. δοκεῖ δὲ καὶ
πρὸς ἀλήθειαν ἅπασαν ἡ γνῶσις αὐτῆς μεγάλα συμβάλλεσθαι,
μάλιστα δὲ πρὸς τὴν φύσιν· ἔστι γὰρ οἷον ἀρχὴ
τῶν ζῴων. ἐπιζητοῦμεν δὲ θεωρῆσαι καὶ γνῶναι τήν τε φύσιν
αὐτῆς καὶ τὴν οὐσίαν, εἶθ' ὅσα συμβέβηκε περὶ αὐτήν·
ὧν τὰ μὲν ἴδια πάθη τῆς ψυχῆς εἶναι δοκεῖ, τὰ δὲ δι'
ἐκείνην καὶ τοῖς ζῴοις ὑπάρχειν. πάντῃ δὲ πάντως ἐστὶ τῶν
χαλεπωτάτων λαβεῖν τινα πίστιν περὶ αὐτῆς. καὶ γάρ, ὄντος
κοινοῦ τοῦ ζητήματος καὶ πολλοῖς ἑτέροις, λέγω δὲ τοῦ περὶ
τὴν οὐσίαν καὶ τὸ τί ἐστι, τάχ' ἄν τῳ δόξειε μία τις εἶναι
μέθοδος κατὰ πάντων περὶ ὧν βουλόμεθα γνῶναι τὴν οὐσίαν,
ὥσπερ καὶ τῶν κατὰ συμβεβηκὸς ἰδίων ἀπόδειξις,
ὥστε ζητητέον ἂν εἴη τὴν μέθοδον ταύτην· εἰ δὲ μὴ ἔστι μία
τις καὶ κοινὴ μέθοδος περὶ τὸ τί ἐστιν, ἔτι χαλεπώτερον
γίνεται τὸ πραγματευθῆναι· δεήσει γὰρ λαβεῖν περὶ ἕκαστον
τίς ὁ τρόπος, ἐὰν δὲ φανερὸν ᾖ πότερον ἀπόδειξίς
ἐστιν ἢ διαίρεσις ἢ καί τις ἄλλη μέθοδος, ἔτι πολλὰς
ἀπορίας ἔχει καὶ πλάνας, ἐκ τίνων δεῖ ζητεῖν· ἄλλαι γὰρ
ἄλλων ἀρχαί, καθάπερ ἀριθμῶν καὶ ἐπιπέδων.
πρῶτον δ' ἴσως ἀναγκαῖον διελεῖν ἐν τίνι τῶν γενῶν καὶ τί
ἐστι, λέγω δὲ πότερον τόδε τι καὶ οὐσία ἢ ποιὸν ἢ ποσόν, ἢ καί τις
ἄλλη τῶν διαιρεθεισῶν κατηγοριῶν, ἔτι δὲ πότερον τῶν ἐν
δυνάμει ὄντων ἢ μᾶλλον ἐντελέχειά τις· διαφέρει γὰρ οὔ τι
μικρόν. σκεπτέον δὲ καὶ εἰ μεριστὴ ἢ ἀμερής, καὶ πότερον
ὁμοειδὴς ἅπασα ψυχὴ ἢ οὔ· εἰ δὲ μὴ ὁμοειδής, πότερον
εἴδει διαφέρουσα ἢ γένει. νῦν μὲν γὰρ οἱ λέγοντες καὶ ζητοῦντες
περὶ ψυχῆς περὶ τῆς ἀνθρωπίνης μόνης ἐοίκασιν ἐπισκοπεῖν·
εὐλαβητέον δ' ὅπως μὴ λανθάνῃ πότερον εἷς ὁ λόγος
αὐτῆς ἐστι, καθάπερ ζῴου, ἢ καθ' ἕκαστον ἕτερος, οἷον
ἵππου, κυνός, ἀνθρώπου, θεοῦ, τὸ δὲ ζῷον τὸ καθόλου ἤτοι οὐθέν
ἐστιν ἢ ὕστερον, ὁμοίως δὲ κἂν εἴ τι κοινὸν ἄλλο κατηγοροῖτο·
ἔτι δέ, εἰ μὴ πολλαὶ ψυχαὶ ἀλλὰ μόρια, πότερον δεῖ
ζητεῖν πρότερον τὴν ὅλην ψυχὴν ἢ τὰ μόρια. χαλεπὸν δὲ καὶ
τούτων διορίσαι ποῖα πέφυκεν ἕτερα ἀλλήλων, καὶ πότερον
τὰ μόρια χρὴ ζητεῖν πρότερον ἢ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν, οἷον τὸ
νοεῖν ἢ τὸν νοῦν, καὶ τὸ αἰσθάνεσθαι ἢ τὸ αἰσθητικόν· ὁμοίως
δὲ καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν ἄλλων. εἰ δὲ τὰ ἔργα πρότερον, πάλιν ἄν τις
ἀπορήσειεν εἰ τὰ ἀντικείμενα πρότερον τούτων ζητητέον, οἷον
τὸ αἰσθητὸν τοῦ αἰσθητικοῦ, καὶ τὸ νοητὸν τοῦ νοῦ. ἔοικε δ'
οὐ μόνον τὸ τί ἐστι γνῶναι χρήσιμον εἶναι πρὸς τὸ θεωρῆσαι
τὰς αἰτίας τῶν συμβεβηκότων ταῖς οὐσίαις (ὥσπερ ἐν τοῖς
μαθήμασι τί τὸ εὐθὺ καὶ τὸ καμπύλον, ἢ τί γραμμὴ καὶ ἐπίπεδον,
πρὸς τὸ κατιδεῖν πόσαις ὀρθαῖς αἱ τοῦ τριγώνου γωνίαι
ἴσαι), ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀνάπαλιν τὰ συμβεβηκότα συμβάλλεται
μέγα μέρος πρὸς τὸ εἰδέναι τὸ τί ἐστιν· ἐπειδὰν γὰρ ἔχωμεν
ἀποδιδόναι κατὰ τὴν φαντασίαν περὶ τῶν συμβεβηκότων,
ἢ πάντων ἢ τῶν πλείστων, τότε καὶ περὶ τῆς οὐσίας
ἕξομεν λέγειν κάλλιστα· πάσης γὰρ ἀποδείξεως ἀρχὴ τὸ
τί ἐστιν, ὥστε καθ' ὅσους τῶν ὁρισμῶν μὴ συμβαίνει τὰ συμβεβηκότα
γνωρίζειν, ἀλλὰ μηδ' εἰκάσαι περὶ αὐτῶν εὐμαρές,
δῆλον ὅτι διαλεκτικῶς εἴρηνται καὶ κενῶς ἅπαντες.
ἀπορίαν δ' ἔχει καὶ τὰ πάθη τῆς ψυχῆς, πότερόν ἐστι πάντα
κοινὰ καὶ τοῦ ἔχοντος ἢ ἔστι τι καὶ τῆς ψυχῆς ἴδιον
αὐτῆς· τοῦτο γὰρ λαβεῖν μὲν ἀναγκαῖον, οὐ ῥᾴδιον δέ. φαίνεται
δὲ τῶν μὲν πλείστων οὐθὲν ἄνευ τοῦ σώματος πάσχειν οὐδὲ
ποιεῖν, οἷον ὀργίζεσθαι, θαρρεῖν, ἐπιθυμεῖν, ὅλως αἰσθάνεσθαι,
μάλιστα δ' ἔοικεν ἰδίῳ τὸ νοεῖν· εἰ δ' ἐστὶ καὶ τοῦτο φαντασία
τις ἢ μὴ ἄνευ φαντασίας, οὐκ ἐνδέχοιτ' ἂν οὐδὲ τοῦτ' ἄνευ
σώματος εἶναι. εἰ μὲν οὖν ἔστι τι τῶν τῆς ψυχῆς ἔργων ἢ
παθημάτων ἴδιον, ἐνδέχοιτ' ἂν αὐτὴν χωρίζεσθαι· εἰ δὲ μηθέν
ἐστιν ἴδιον αὐτῆς, οὐκ ἂν εἴη χωριστή, ἀλλὰ καθάπερ τῷ

en.402a1: Holding as we do that, while knowledge of any kind is a thing to be honoured and prized,
en.402a2: one kind of it may, either by reason of its greater exactness or of a higher dignity
en.402a3: and greater wonderfulness in its objects, be more honourable and precious than another, on both
en.402a4: accounts we should naturally be led to place in the front rank the study of the soul.
en.402a5: The knowledge of the soul admittedly contributes greatly to the advance of truth in general,
en.402a6: and, above all, to our understanding of Nature, for the soul is in some
en.402a7: sense the principle of animal life. Our aim is to grasp and understand, first its essential
en.402a8: nature, and secondly its properties; of these some are thought to be affections
en.402a9: proper to the soul itself, while others are considered to attach to the animal
en.402a10:
owing to the presence within it of soul.
To attain any assured knowledge
en.402a11: about the soul is one of the most difficult things in the world. As the
en.402a12: form of question which here presents itself, viz. the question 'What is it?',
en.402a13: recurs in other fields, it might be supposed that there was some single
en.402a14: method of inquiry applicable to all objects whose essential nature
en.402a15: we are endeavouring to ascertain (as there is for derived properties the single method
en.402a16: of demonstration); in that case what we should have to seek for would be this unique method. But if
en.402a17: there is no such single and general method for solving the question of essence, our task becomes still
en.402a18: more difficult; in the case of each different subject we shall have to determine the appropriate
en.402a19: process of investigation. If to this there be a clear answer, e.g. that the process
en.402a20: is demonstration or division, or some other known method, difficulties and hesitations
en.402a21: still beset us-with what facts shall we begin the inquiry? For the facts which form the starting-points
en.402a22: in different subjects must be different, as e.g. in the case
en.402a23:
of numbers and surfaces.
First, no doubt, it is necessary to determine in which of the summa
en.402a24: genera soul lies, what it is; is it 'a this-somewhat, 'a substance, or is it a quale or a quantum, or some
en.402a25: other of the remaining kinds of predicates which we have distinguished? Further, does soul belong to the class of
en.402a26: potential existents, or is it not rather an actuality? Our answer to this question is of the greatest importance.
en.402b1: We must consider also whether soul is divisible or is without parts, and whether it
en.402b2: is everywhere homogeneous or not; and if not homogeneous, whether its various
en.402b3: forms are different specifically or generically: up to the present time those who have discussed
en.402b4: and investigated soul seem to have confined themselves to the human soul.
en.402b5: We must be careful not to ignore the question whether soul can be defined in a single unambiguous
en.402b6: formula, as is the case with animal, or whether we must not give a separate formula for
en.402b7: each sort of it, as we do for horse, dog, man, god (in the latter case the 'universal' animal-and so too every
en.402b8: other 'common predicate'-being treated either as nothing at all or as a later product). Further, if what exists
en.402b9: is not a plurality of souls, but a plurality of parts of one soul, which ought we to
en.402b10: investigate first, the whole soul or its parts? (It is also a difficult problem
en.402b11: to decide which of these parts are in nature distinct from one another.)
en.402b12: Again, which ought we to investigate first, these parts or
en.402b13: their functions, mind or thinking, the faculty or the act of sensation, and
en.402b14: so on? If the investigation of the functions precedes that of the parts,
en.402b15: the further question suggests itself: ought we not before either
en.402b16: to consider the correlative objects, e.g. of sense or thought? It
en.402b17: seems not only useful for the discovery of the causes of the derived
en.402b18: properties of substances to be acquainted with the essential
en.402b19: nature of those substances (as in mathematics it is useful
en.402b20: for the understanding of the property of the equality of the interior angles of a triangle to
en.402b21: two right angles to know the essential nature of the straight and the curved or of the
en.402b22: line and the plane) but also conversely, for the knowledge of the essential nature of a substance is
en.402b23: largely promoted by an acquaintance with its properties: for, when we are able to give an
en.402b24: account conformable to experience of all or most of the properties of a substance,
en.402b25: we shall be in the most favourable position to say something worth saying about the essential nature
en.402b26: of that subject; in all demonstration a definition of the essence is required as a starting-point, so that definitions
en.403a1: which do not enable us to discover the derived properties, or which fail to facilitate
en.403a2: even a conjecture about them, must obviously, one and all, be dialectical and futile.
en.403a3: A further problem presented by the affections of soul is this: are they all affections of the
en.403a4: complex of body and soul, or is there any one among them peculiar to the soul
en.403a5: by itself? To determine this is indispensable but difficult. If we consider the majority
en.403a6: of them, there seems to be no case in which the soul can act or be acted
en.403a7: upon without involving the body; e.g. anger, courage, appetite, and sensation generally.
en.403a8: Thinking seems the most probable exception; but if this too proves to be a form
en.403a9: of imagination or to be impossible without imagination, it too requires
en.403a10: a body as a condition of its existence. If there is any way of acting
en.403a11: or being acted upon proper to soul, soul will be capable of separate existence;
en.403a12: if there is none, its separate existence is impossible.
